questions.q: What does the AFTER clause do when creating a task?
options: Declares that the task should run only after another named task completes
Schedules the task to run at a fixed time every day
Deletes the task after it runs once
Grants a role permission to view the task
questions.explain: AFTER names a dependency — the task only runs once the task(s) it depends on have completed.

questions.q: In a Task Graph, which task has its own SCHEDULE?
options: Only the root task — every dependent task runs when its predecessor finishes, not on a clock
Every task in the graph has an identical schedule
Only the last task in the chain
None of the tasks have schedules in a graph
questions.explain: Only the root task is time-scheduled; dependent tasks trigger off their predecessor completing, via AFTER.

questions.q: What does Snowsight's Graph tab show for a task with dependents?
options: A visual DAG of the whole chain — which tasks feed into which
A billing summary for the warehouse running the tasks
A list of every user who has ever queried the account
Nothing — Snowsight has no visualization for task chains
questions.explain: The Graph tab visualizes the full dependency chain as a DAG, similar in shape to an Airflow DAG or ADF pipeline.

questions.q: Why isn't resuming only the root task enough to run a full Task Graph?
options: Every task in the chain is created suspended and must be individually resumed for the graph to run end to end
Resuming the root task automatically resumes every dependent task too
Task Graphs cannot be resumed at all once suspended
Only the last task in the chain needs to be resumed
questions.explain: Every task starts suspended, including dependents — the whole chain needs resuming, from the bottom up, for it to actually execute.

questions.q: What does Snowsight's 'Execute Task Graph' option do?
options: Manually triggers the entire task chain on demand, useful for testing before trusting the schedule
Permanently deletes the entire task chain
Automatically writes documentation for the pipeline
Converts the task chain into a stored procedure
questions.explain: It lets you manually kick off the whole graph immediately, rather than waiting for the root task's schedule to fire.
